categories.main_business_segments: Henan Jindan Lactic Acid Technology Co., Ltd. primarily engages in the research, production, and sales of lactic acid and its derivatives, including lactic acid salts such as sodium lactate and calcium lactate. The company also extends into the production of biodegradable materials like polylactic acid (PLA) and related bio-based polymers. It operates in the food manufacturing sector, specifically in fermented products and seasoning manufacturing, with a focus on organic acids within fermentation industry sub-sectors.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company utilizes microbial fermentation technology based on corn starch as raw material to produce lactic acid and its derivatives. It integrates traditional fermentation with modern biotechnology and chemical engineering techniques. Key technological focuses include strain improvement, fermentation process optimization, extraction and purification technologies, and polymerization for biodegradable plastics. The company also develops advanced fermentation equipment and engages in research on bio-degradable polymer modification and application.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Jindan serves a diverse customer base across food, feed, pharmaceutical, chemical, and biodegradable materials industries. Its lactic acid products are used as acidulants, preservatives, pH regulators, and flavor enhancers in food and beverage sectors, as well as in animal feed acidifiers and preservatives. The company also supplies raw materials for biodegradable plastics used in packaging, textiles, agriculture, and medical applications. Major customers include well-known enterprises such as Dupont, Henan Shuanghui, Yili, and Mengniu, spanning domestic and international markets.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates primarily in China, with its headquarters and main production facilities located in Henan Province, a major corn-producing region. It has established a sales network covering almost all provinces in China and exports products to over 90 countries and regions worldwide, including Europe, Japan, South Korea, Southeast Asia, the Americas, and Oceania. It also has a subsidiary in the Netherlands to support its European market presence.
categories.supply_chain_position: Jindan operates mainly in the midstream segment of the lactic acid industry supply chain, focusing on the fermentation production of lactic acid and its derivatives. It is actively extending its operations upstream into corn cultivation and starch processing through its agricultural subsidiary and downstream into biodegradable polymer production and modification, forming an integrated circular industrial chain from corn to starch, lactic acid, lactate salts, lactide, PLA, PBAT, and biodegradable composite materials.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company prioritizes innovation in strain development, fermentation processes, extraction technologies, and polymerization for biodegradable materials. It invests in R&D projects targeting low pH fermentation, neutral agent-free lactic acid production, lignocellulosic biomass fermentation, and high-performance PLA resin development. Jindan emphasizes building a circular bio-based materials industry chain and enhancing product quality and cost efficiency. Collaboration with universities and research institutes supports its technology advancement and new product development.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through the direct sale of lactic acid, lactic acid salts, and related by-products. The company employs a mixed sales model with direct sales to strategic customers and distributor-based sales domestically and internationally. It also derives income from government subsidies and investment returns, including financial product gains. The business model is product sales-centric, with no significant reliance on subscription or licensing.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Jindan is a leading domestic player in the lactic acid industry, ranking among the top producers in China with an annual capacity of 183,000 tons. Globally, it competes with major companies like Corbion (Netherlands) and NatureWorks (USA), which dominate about 50% of global capacity. Domestically, it competes with companies such as Fengyuan Group and Haizheng Biomaterials. Jindan leverages its technological capabilities, integrated supply chain, and broad customer base to maintain a strong market position amid increasing competition and capacity expansions.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, the company reported operating revenue of approximately RMB 1.505 billion, representing a 6.15% increase year-over-year. However, net profit attributable to shareholders declined by 56.01% to RMB 37.49 million, mainly due to significant asset impairment provisions. Total assets reached RMB 3.46 billion, with a slight growth of 1.75%. The company’s cash flow from operating activities improved substantially by 634.96%, reflecting better working capital management. Overall, Jindan is a mid-sized enterprise with steady revenue growth but facing profitability pressure.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Jindan emphasizes its comprehensive industrial chain integration from raw material sourcing to advanced biodegradable materials, providing cost and quality advantages. Its proprietary fermentation technologies, strain improvements, and extraction methods enable efficient, environmentally friendly production. The company’s products are certified for food safety and quality, serving diverse applications from food additives to high-performance biodegradable plastics. Its strong R&D capabilities and strategic partnerships support continuous innovation, enabling it to offer differentiated, high-value bio-based products that meet evolving market and regulatory demands.
